item.title: Developing solutions without fully understanding users' problems is something I've made many mistakes in.
item.description:
1. Do consumers recognize that they have the problem you are trying to solve?

2. If there was a solution, would they buy it?

3. Would they buy it from us?

4. Can we build a solution for that problem?" The common tendency of product development is to skip straight to the fourth question and build a solution before confirming that customers have the problem.

item.title: The Truth of the World is Intentionally Erased and Shielded
item.description: His mind was more or less pure, with no knowledge of those “unspoken words” and never “contaminated” by real social life. The world as seen through a child’s eyes is unreal; it is an imaginary world that has been instilled into their minds. When they grow up and encounter society in the future, they will discover that what they thought was true when they were children is absurd and ridiculous in reality. +++

item.title: From the perspective of programmers, it is obvious that wealth is created.
item.description: Hearing that the richest 5% of people own more than half of society’s wealth often leads to the conclusion that this is unfair. An experienced programmer might also find this unfair because the top 5% of programmers write 99% of the world’s excellent software. +++
